# Ravi Vellanki

Business development contact at a diagnostics company working on cfDNA-based recurrence monitoring. External contact; no affiliation hub in this vault.

## Role

Ravi approached Ines after the [[halo-annual-meeting-2026]] about licensing or co-developing the [[fragmentomics-classifier]] once it is locked and validated. There is no agreement; one exploratory call took place on 2026-07-02, with the institute technology transfer office present.

## How We Work Together

All contact is in writing or with the technology transfer office present. Ines declared the contact on the institute conflict-of-interest register on 2026-07-03. Because his company could later request access to institute data, Ines will recuse from any [[data-governance-board-membership|data governance board]] item involving it. Nothing about St Aldric data, unpublished results or the Halo truth set is shared with him. The rules are in [[conflict-of-interest-handling-vendor-contacts]].

## Current Threads

- Waiting until the [[mrd-manuscript]] is accepted before any further discussion; Ines told him so in July.
- His company has asked whether it could join Halo as an industry partner. That is a question for [[henrik-dahl]] and the Halo steering committee, not for Ines alone.

## History

The first contact came after Ines's talk at the [[halo-annual-meeting-2026]] in June 2026, by email to her and [[maximilian-auer]]. Ines answered that the classifier is not locked, that external validation is pending, and that any commercial discussion would involve the institute's technology transfer office. The exploratory call on 2026-07-02 covered only public information: the preprint and the conference talk.

## Boundaries

Ravi is courteous and clear about his company's interest, which makes the boundaries easy to state. The St Aldric consent form has no clause on commercial use ([[st-aldric-consent-wording]]), so any future arrangement would be built on new consent, a licence to the method, or validation on other cohorts. Ines has also decided not to discuss the [[data-access-policy-revision]] with him at all while she drafts it, since the clause could later govern requests from his company.
